ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, banking and licensing, screen all shareholders, directors, authorized signatories, beneficial owners, intermediaries and key counterparties against United Nations sanctions, European Union sanctions, Spanish domestic sanctions and law-enforcement notices, OFAC lists as an additional risk control, applicable UK sanctions where relevant, and reputable adverse-media databases. Apply enhanced due diligence to PEPs, former PEPs, close family members and known close associates under Law 10/2010. Verify identity, ownership chain, control rights, source of wealth, source of funds, purpose of the relationship and expected transaction profile. Do not rely solely on name matching; resolve aliases, transliteration differences and false positives. Escalate potential matches, prohibit tipping-off, document the decision and file a suspicious transaction report with SEPBLAC where legally required. For intraocular-lens manufacturing, also screen distributors, hospitals, agents and importers because medical-device supply chains create elevated bribery, procurement and diversion risks.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central official electronic services portal: https://sede.registradores.org/; the relevant authority is the Registro Mercantil Central
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be distinct from existing registered names, must include the required legal-form indication or accepted abbreviation such as Sociedad Limitada or S.L., and must not be misleading or contrary to law, public order or public interest. Spanish is accepted nationally; names may contain foreign-language terms where legally acceptable and sufficiently distinctive. Local-script naming is not generally mandatory for a Spanish company. Foreign words, transliterations and acronyms remain subject to distinctiveness, legality and non-confusion review. The name certificate is generally valid for three months for execution of the incorporation deed, while the reservation is generally maintained for six months; the 30-day workflow target should not be treated as the statutory Spanish validity period.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names identical or confusingly similar to existing registered company names
Terms implying an official state, autonomous-community, municipal or public-authority status without authorization
Banco, banking, bank or equivalent regulated-finance terminology without required authorization
Insurance, insurer, aseguradora, credit institution, securities-market or investment-fund terminology without authorization
National, España, Spanish state, Instituto, Real, Crown, Royal or equivalent protected or official-sounding terms where prior authorization is required
Terms suggesting a regulated medical, pharmaceutical or healthcare authority, public body or official certification without a lawful basis
Obscene, discriminatory, unlawful, deceptive or public-order-offensive terms
Names conflicting with protected trademarks, trade names or other industrial-property rights
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Obtain a negative company-name certificate from the Registro Mercantil Central before signing the incorporation deed. If rejected, identify whether the ground is identity, similarity, prohibited terminology, insufficient legal-form indication or formal defect; revise the proposed name and submit alternatives. An administrative challenge or reconsideration should be filed with the issuing authority within the applicable procedural period stated in the rejection notice, supported by evidence of distinctiveness, authorization, prior rights or corrected wording. If the rejection is maintained, pursue the legally available judicial review before the competent administrative court within the time limit stated in the decision. Because company-name review is highly formal and similarity-based, filing corrected alternatives is usually faster than litigating. A trademark clearance at the Spanish Patent and Trademark Office and EUIPO should be completed separately; a company-name certificate does not create trademark rights.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office in Spain is required and must permit receipt of legal and administrative notices. A serviced or virtual office may be acceptable for a holding, consulting or early administrative phase if the provider permits legal domicile, mail handling, identification of the tenant and access for authorities. It is not adequate as the sole operational site for high-precision manufacture of intraocular lenses. The company should maintain a genuine production, quality-control, storage and record-access location appropriate to Regulation (EU) 2017/745 on medical devices, Spanish medical-device rules and AEMPS oversight. Manufacturing premises, quality systems, technical documentation, traceability and post-market surveillance must be operational before commercial production.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 10-25 percent during ordinary pre-incorporation or tax onboarding absent red flags; materially higher, approximately 30-60 percent, after a licensing, medical-device, customs, tax, AML or complaint trigger. These are risk estimates, not statutory probabilities. AEMPS, regional authorities, tax authorities, customs and labor or occupational-safety authorities may conduct announced or unannounced inspections within their legal powers. A virtual office without demonstrable manufacturing substance presents a high adverse finding risk.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital – LSC): Título II, arts. 20–34 (incorporation, public deed, registration); arts. 54–58 (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada); art. 4 (minimum capital EUR 3,000); arts. 62–63 (bank deposit certificate); Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (RD 1784/1996).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry of the registered-office province); name certification issued by the Registro Mercantil Central; supervisory control by the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado (DGRN).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (notarized public deed of incorporation) followed by mandatory inscription in the Registro Mercantil, which confers legal personality (art. 33 LSC).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 3,000 minimum share capital, fully subscribed and fully paid up at formation (LSC art. 4); cash contributions deposited in a Spanish bank account and evidenced by a bank deposit certificate issued within two months before the deed (LSC arts. 62–63); in-kind contributions described and valued in the deed; no separate escrow account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporators ratify the execution of the incorporation deed of [Company], S.L., confirm the subscription and full payment of the EUR 3,000 share capital, and adopt [address], [city], Spain, as the registered office. IT IS FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed Sole Director (Administrador Único) with the widest corporate, banking and litigation powers, and [Name] appointed as non-statutory Company Secretary. IT IS FURTHER RESOLVED, to open corporate bank accounts, apply for the provisional tax identification number (NIF), legalize the corporate books, execute all state, regional and municipal registrations, and obtain the industrial, AEMPS and environmental authorizations required to commence manufacturing of intraocular acrylic lenses. All prior acts are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of Corporate Name (Certificado de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) – electronic office of the Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit, via the MRC online portal, a request listing three alternative proposed company names in the format '[Name], S.L.'; pay the official fee; the Central Registry verifies that no identical or confusingly similar name exists and issues the negative name certificate, valid for three non-renewable months.
required_dossiers: Official application form (Modelo de denominación social)
Payment receipt of the official fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If one or more proposed names are denied (identity, similarity, prohibited terms), file a fresh application with alternative names; the fee is non-refundable but reprocessing follows the same SLA; an appeal to the DGRN is available if the refusal is unjustified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Pre-Incorporation Bank Account and Deposit of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution licensed by the Banco de España
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional account in the name of the future company and deposit at least EUR 3,000; obtain the bank deposit certificate (certificado bancario de desembolso) identifying the holder, depositor, and balance; the certificate must be dated within two months prior to the notarial deed (LSC art. 62).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account on AML grounds, submit enhanced KYC documentation or select another institution; alternatively, deposit the funds with the notary's deposit account (cuenta notarial) and obtain a notarial certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Public Deed of Incorporation (Escritura de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary (Notario) competent in the territory of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary with the name certificate, bank deposit certificate, and fully drafted Articles of Association; the notary verifies identity, capacity, legality of the object clause (manufacture of intraocular lenses, ISIC 3250) and apportions participation quotas; the deed is read and signed; the notary simultaneously requests the provisional NIF from AEAT (art. 33 LSC; art. 18 RD 1777/2004).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses authorization due to unlawful clauses, amend the estatutos and re-notarize; if additional anti-money-laundering information is required, provide it and reschedule; a defective or partial deed must be re-executed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF Provisional) – Modelo 036
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – local tax office or Sede Electrónica
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Modelo 036 together with the first copy of the deed and the notary's certification; AEAT assigns a provisional NIF valid six months, convertible to a definitive NIF upon commercial registration; from this point the company assumes tax filing obligations.
required_dossiers: Modelo 036 signed by the legal representative
Primera copia of the Escritura de Constitución
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT suspends or denies the provisional NIF, rectify the Modelo 036 data and resubmit with corrected deed extracts; in urgent cases request a cita previa appointment for expedited NIF assignment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Transfer and Stamp Duty – Actos Jurídicos Documentados (Modelo 600)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Tributaria / Consejería de Hacienda of the Autonomous Community of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 business days of the deed, self-assess and pay AJD duty on the subscribed capital (0.5%–2% depending on region, typically 1%) using Modelo 600; obtain the justificante de pago to be attached to the registry application.
required_dossiers: Copy of the Escritura de Constitución
Computation of the tax base (nominal capital)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the regional tax office issues an erroneous liquidation, file a solicitud de rectificación de autoliquidación with supporting documents; pay promptly to avoid surcharges and request deferral only if strictly necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Provincial Commercial Registry and Post-Registration Formalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial del domicilio social
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the second copy of the deed with the paid Modelo 600 and provisional NIF; the registrar califica the deed for legality within approximately 15 working days; upon inscription the company acquires legal personality; immediately convert to the definitive NIF (Modelo 036), legalize the corporate books (Libro de Socios, Libro de Actas, Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales) at the same registry, and register in the INE Directory of Companies.
required_dossiers: Segunda copia de la Escritura de Constitución
Certificate of domiciliation of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a suspension or refusal (calificación negativa), remedy the deficiencies through a supplementary corrective deed (escritura de subsanación) or margin notes; appeal to the DGRN within two months of the registration decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Secretaría General de Industria y de la PYME (Ministerio de Industria, Comercio y Turismo) – Registro Integrado Industrial; Consejería de Industria of the relevant Autonomous Community; AEMPS (Agencia Española de Medicamentos y Productos Sanitarios) – medical device establishment registration; Ayuntamiento – municipal Licencia de Actividad/Apertura.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Comunicación de Inicio de Actividad e Inscripción en el Registro de Establecimientos de Productos Sanitarios (AEMPS) + Licencia Municipal de Apertura y Funcionamiento de Establecimiento Industrial + Notified Body CE marking for Class III intraocular lenses under EU Regulation 2017/745 with ISO 13485 quality management system certification.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Órgano Ambiental competente de la Comunidad Autónoma (Consejería de Medio Ambiente) in coordination with the municipal environmental licensing authority (Ayuntamiento).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Simplified Environmental Impact Assessment (Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental Simplificada) under Ley 21/2013, Annex II, Group 9, for plastics-manufacturing installations exceeding regulatory capacity thresholds; below thresholds, municipal environmental license (Licencia Ambiental / Actividades Clasificadas) is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater to municipal sewer: RD 817/2015 limit values and municipal by-laws (indicative: pH 6–9; BOD5 ≤ 300 mg/L; COD ≤ 750 mg/L; TSS ≤ 500 mg/L); discharge to public hydraulic domain requires RD 817/2015 emission limit values. VOC/solvent emissions: RD 117/2003 Solvent Management Plan when consumption ≥ 1 t/yr. Waste handling (polymer scrap and solvents): Ley 7/2022 and RD 553/2020 hazardous waste traceability.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance: compliance certificate with CTE DB-SI (fire protection, evacuation routes) plus periodic municipal fire inspection; structural and load-bearing inspection for lathe machines and cleanroom per municipal building code (ITE); occupational risk prevention plan under Ley 31/1995 with workplace clearance by the Inspección de Trabajo; cleanroom area classified per ISO 14644 if aseptic manufacturing of sterile IOLs is declared.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – sede electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity forming or acquiring a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) must obtain a Spanish tax identification number (NIF) for the company. Process: (1) Obtain a provisional NIF from the AEAT Central Registry of Foreign Taxpayers before formal incorporation or through the notary/Registro Mercantil filing; (2) After registration, the entity is issued the definitive NIF (letter and 8 digits). For VAT purposes, the entity must separately register for the Census VAT roll (Censo de Obligados Tributarios) using model 036/037, declaring commencement of activity in manufacturing under CNAE 3250. Non-resident directors and shareholders may require an NIF or NIE depending on the act performed. No minimum capital is required for an SL, but all contributions must be bank-certified. The registration application must include the intended economic activity, place of establishment, and expected export operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain generally does not permit U.S.-style check-the-box pass-through elections for SLs; the SL is a capital company subject to Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) on worldwide income if managed from or incorporated under Spanish law. Relevant statutory elections: (a) the freedom to elect a fiscal year matching the calendar year under the Corporate Income Tax Law (Article 21 LIS) except for certain group entities; (b) the application of the consolidation regime for tax groups under article 58 and following of the LIS; (c) the EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive / ATAD-mandated controlled-foreign-company rules and hybrid mismatch election disclosures under DAC6 for cross-border arrangements; (d) eligibility to elect the reduced effective tax rate under the Patent Box regime and partial exemption of intra-group dividends under the participation exemption regime. No hybrid-mismatch neutralization election beyond the statutory conflict rules is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: General regime: no registration threshold – any person carrying out a taxable economic activity in Spanish territory must register for VAT from the first taxable transaction. Intra-Community distance sales thresholds: EUR 10,000 for EU-wide distance sales triggers Spanish VAT registration unless the OSS regime is used. Manufacturers exporting intraocular acrylic lenses (ISIC 3250) normally must register for Spanish VAT immediately upon commencing operations. Exception: small businesses using the recargo de equivalencia or simplified scheme have specific annual volume thresholds, but these are not applicable to an SL-exporter under the general VAT regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing (factura electrónica) is mandatory between businesses and with the public administration. For B2B transactions, the 'Ley Crea y Crece' (Law 18/2022) mandates structured electronic invoicing with a private digital platform; all invoices must be machine-readable using European standard EN 16931. The AEAT is progressively introducing the Veri*Factu system for invoice software, requiring certification of billing software and QR/XML submission of invoice facts to the tax authority. Large companies subject to the Immediate Supply of Information (SII) must report invoice data in near-real time using web services (API). Digital stamping or fiscal signature is required for invoices issued through certified Veri*Factu software. For exporters, all export invoices must be issued electronically and linked to the corresponding customs export documentation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported outside the European Union (third-country exports) are subject to 0% VAT (exempt with credit, i.e., zero-rated) provided the following are met: (a) the goods are physically exported from Spain within the period defined by customs law; (b) the supplier is the exporter or acts as such; (c) the export is evidenced by a valid customs export declaration and transport documents; (d) the goods are sold to a customer outside the EU; (e) in the case of contract manufacturing for a third-country customer, the goods must leave the EU customs territory. Intra-Community triangular sales to EU customers may also qualify for zero-rating under the VAT Directive if the customer provides a valid EU VAT number and goods are transported between Member States. Intraocular acrylic lenses destined for surgical implantation are generally taxed as ordinary goods; no medical zero-rating is automatic without export evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA – Documento Único Administrativo) with export customs entry and AEAT validation date
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport document proving actual dispatch from the EU
Commercial invoice issued in accordance with Spanish VAT regulations
Proof of payment and Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas) or equivalent SWIFT/Letter of Credit settlement evidence
Export license and health/technical sanctions evidence for medical devices under Regulation (EU) 2017/745
Incoterms documentary evidence (e.g., CIP, CIF, FOB contract and insurance certificate where applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEAT Customs and Excise Audit and VAT audit services scrutinize export zero-rating claims through documentary verification and cross-border data analytics. If an export is found not to have left the EU, or if documentation is false, incomplete, or untimely, the exporter loses the zero-rating and becomes liable for 21% VAT on the supply price, plus late-payment interest. A fraudulent export zero-rating scheme triggers: (a) tax base adjustment and VAT assessment; (b) penalty of 50% to 150% of the VAT amount under article 191 of the General Tax Law, depending on concealment; (c) dual penalties for both failure to issue the DUA and false customs declarations; (d) criminal liability under the Spanish Criminal Code if tax loss exceeds EUR 120,000, with imprisonment of 1 to 5 years; (e) retroactive clawback up to 4 years (or longer but for gross negligence and fraudulent concealment the prescriptive period runs to 10 years in certain customs cases). The exporter must retain the full customs and transport bundle for at least 6 years, and in case of intra-group or related-party exports, the transfer pricing documentation must separately substantiate arm's-length consideration in addition to customs and VAT documentary requirements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem and European System of Central Banks; foreign exchange and capital movement oversight is jointly administered with the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio (Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business) under European capital movement law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for all current and capital transactions. Spain imposes no general exchange controls; capital movements within the EU and with third countries are liberalised pursuant to TFEU Article 63. Profit remittance for foreign direct investors is unrestricted for EU/EEA owners; non-EU investors must comply with foreign investment screening Law 19/2003 (prior notification for investments exceeding EUR 500 million in strategic sectors or 10% voting in listed companies), which is a declarative and approval-for-official-control requirement, not a currency convertibility hurdle. An SL distributing profits must meet Spanish Corporate Law (Law of Capital Companies, Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010) formalities: approved annual accounts, auditor report (if required), and corporate resolution, then remit freely through bank with BOP code 3700.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline applies to export proceeds in foreign currency in Spain. Exporters may hold accounts abroad or retain foreign currency in Spanish accounts without limitation. For trade statistics and tax purposes, all cross-border goods movements must be declared to the Tax Agency (AEAT) using the Intrastat/Customs declarations; a summary declaration on the Single Administrative Document (SAD) and the annual 'Declaración de Operaciones con Pagos Exteriores' (external payments statement) are required, but no forced conversion exists.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR and multicurrency) / Capital Escrow Account (if required)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium with significant regulatory restrictions. Spanish-licensed EMI institutions (or EU EMIs passported under PSD2) may open accounts remotely, provide SEPA transfers and EUR/USD/GBP multi-currency accounts, and offer competitive FX pricing. However, EMIs cannot provideLetter of Credit (import/export) facilities, documentary collections, or trade finance guarantees. For a high-risk medical device manufacturer requiring LCs and cross-border clearing, an EMI can serve as a secondary or payables rail, but a Tier-1 bank is mandatory for core treasury and trade. Non-EU EMIs without a Spanish branch or passport cannot operate.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish Tier-1 banks generally require an in-person KYC interview with at least one director (preferably the CEO or CFO) and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), particularly when the SL has non-resident shareholders. Remote opening is occasionally accepted for low-risk sectors after video identification, the use of a Spanish NIE (foreign person ID), and a Spanish registered address, but for high-risk intraocular lens manufacturing (medical devices with regulatory license) nearly all banks mandate a physical appearance at the local branch or at a notary in Spain. If the director is non-resident, a notarized power of attorney with apostille may be accepted, but the bank will usually appoint a local compliance officer for ongoing monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Origin of initial capital injection from a Latin American buyer (e.g., Colombia, Peru, Mexico) with unclear source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide audited financial statements of the parent/benefactor, shareholders resolution for capital distribution, signed purchase or loan agreement, bank statements from originating bank, tax residency certificate of investor, and a detailed organisational chart with UBO declaration. Include commercial justification for the lens distribution contract and pricing evidence to align with transfer pricing rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Medical device sector deemed high-risk due to public procurement corruption, bribery risk in public hospitals, or sanctions exposure in target markets (e.g., Latin America).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit ISO 13485 certification, EU CE marking (MDR 2017/745), national health registry filings, export licences for each destination country, evidence of local medical device agent, anti-bribery / anti-corruption policy, and completed due diligence on all distributors (including UBO and sanctions screening). Provide a clean compliance declarationand signed distributors' commitment not to pay bribery.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: UBO tax residency in a non-transparent jurisdiction (e.g., low-tax state) leading to FEI/CRS concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a valid tax residency certificate issued by the respective tax authority, CRS self-certification, FATCA status, and underlying business rationale. Include copy of the SL's corporate register deed showing the UBO's role, board resolution for treasury operations, and evidence of substance (office lease, employee payroll, Spanish social security filings).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a foreign direct investment (e.g., parent company injects capital into the Spanish SL), routing is via a SWIFT MT103 wire transfer to the SL's IBAN (ES + 22 digits) at the Spanish bank. Payment purpose must be coded as 'Capital Injection' and, for cross-border from a non-EU country, the corresponding Bank of Spain BOP code (e.g., 3610 - direct investment in Spain via equity capital) must be provided. Prior to execution, the SL* has 30 calendar days to file the foreign investment declaration with the Trade Directorate (Form D-1A) if the investor acquires 10% or more of the registered equity. The bank may require a board resolution approving the capital increase, a notarial deed of the increase, corporate tax ID (CIF/NIF), and the UBO proof. For EU/EEA investors, a prior declaration is not required but a statistics filing is still due. For cash under EUR 10,000, a simplified SEPA transfer is possible; for larger amounts, SWIFT/CHAPS equivalent is mandatory.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For distributor payments or supplier settlements, the principal rails are: (1) SWIFT MT103 direct for invoice payments (must include purchase order, invoice, and shipping documents for customs purposes; BOP purpose code 3300 for goods, 3400 for services). (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) issued via SWIFT MT700, subject to UCP600, for large purchases or to mitigate counterparty risk; Spanish banks typically require 100% collateral or an approved working capital line. (3) For intra-EU settlements, SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) protocol with unique 'CAD' shown in the reference field. Exports to Latin America require montly statistical filing with the AEAT; any payment above EUR 10,000 triggers the 'Form S-1' obligation to report to Banco de España under law 10/2010. For USD settlements, Spanish banks use the Federal Reserve Fedwire/SWIFT network; a correspondent bank in USA (e.g., JPMorgan or Citi) is required. The SL should maintain USD and EUR accounts plus a CLS-generated FX contract to settle daily net positions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CNY) with up to 12 months tenors and tenors renewed only through rollovers at the same bank

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on non-fully-convertible LATAM currencies (COP, PEN, ARS, BRL) executed with Spanish credit entities or international counterparties where deliverability barrier applies
FX currency swaps for a two-way interest/principal exchange (EUR against USD) for trade financing or long-term cash-flow matching
European-style FX options (call/put) for hedging lens export pricing against adverse currency movement while preserving upside for competitive bid pricing
Cross-currency basis swaps to convert USD asset receivables into EUR without re-entering the spot market twice
Market-approved commodity/price hedging does not apply; only pure FX instruments are permitted due to the treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) with annual UBO confirmation statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry of the registered office province (Registro Mercantil Provincial)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' approval by 30 June for calendar-year end; deposit within 1 month after approval, i.e., no later than 31 July. If fiscal year differs, within one month of the general meeting held before the end of the sixth month following the close of each fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: administrative fine from EUR 300 to EUR 2,000 plus interest; continued default triggers 'cierre registral' preventing the company from filing further registrable documents; directors may become jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate debts under Art. 367 Ley de Sociedades de Capital.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Modelo 200) and mandatory related schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the expiration of 6 months after the tax year-end. For calendar-year taxpayers: 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: surcharge of 5% per month up to 20% (voluntary period); after AEAT notification, fine up to 50% of the tax due; delay interest accrues at the statutory annual rate. Failure to file may also trigger criminal penalties for tax fraud if the amount exceeds EUR 120,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Third-Party Information Statement (Modelo 347) for related entities and suppliers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 March of the year following the reporting calendar year. Mandatory only where the aggregate transactions with any one customer/supplier exceed EUR 3,005.06, or if government subsidies exceed this amount.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission or late filing: penalty of EUR 150 to EUR 5,000 per data item, subject to a minimum of 0.5% of the omitted transaction value; also loss of tax deduction rights for incomplete or inaccurate data.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalization of Mandatory Corporate and Accounting Books (Libros Obligatorios: inventory, annual accounts, minutes, members register, directors register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) – corporate book legalization office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months following the close of the financial year, before the books are deemed presented; for calendar-year end, by 30 April of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-legalized books have no evidentiary value in court and cannot be used to certify corporate decisions; fines up to EUR 6,000 under the Spanish Tax Act for obstruction; annual accounts deposit may be rejected until books are regularized.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada when, for at least two consecutive financial years, it meets at least two of the following three thresholds: total assets exceed EUR 4,000,000; net annual turnover exceeds EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees exceeds 50. Audit is also mandatory when the SL is a parent company of a group required to present consolidated accounts, when it is a public-interest entity, or when otherwise required by sectoral regulation (e.g., financial or medical device licensing condition).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad, PGC) in accordance with EU Directives; for individual annual accounts of an SL, local GAAP (PGC) applies. If consolidated financial statements are prepared, IFRS as adopted by the EU is mandatory.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must submit a 'Declaración de Titular Real' to the Mercantile Registry whenever there is a change of beneficial ownership, within 30 days. As part of the annual accounts deposit, a renewed UBO statement must be filed (or confirmed as unchanged) with the Registro Mercantil. The statement must identify each individual who directly or indirectly holds more than 25% of the capital, voting rights, or who ultimately exercises control. Failure to comply may result in penalties from EUR 1,500 to EUR 60,000 and a 'cierre registral' blocking future filings.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores)
Statutory accounting books (Libro de Inventario y Cuentas Anuales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 400 – 800 USD per annum (EUR 350 – 750 typical for professional registered office and corporate secretarial agent in Spain)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 4,900 – 10,300 USD per annum (EUR 4,500 – 9,500 typical certified audit fee for a medium-sized manufacturing SL subject to mandatory audit)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general rate for Spanish resident companies, including a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada. Newly incorporated entities generally qualify for a 15% rate in the first profitable tax period and the following period, subject to statutory exclusions and eligibility conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax incentives may include the 15% rate for qualifying newly created entities and qualifying start-ups, research and development deductions, technological innovation deductions, deductions for investments in qualifying audiovisual and cultural productions, employment-related incentives, and participation-exemption relief for qualifying dividends and capital gains. The general participation exemption is subject to statutory ownership, holding-period, anti-hybrid, and minimum-taxation conditions. Regional incentives may differ in the Basque Country and Navarre; the ordinary national regime applies to a company resident outside those territories.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Impuesto sobre Sociedades e Impuesto sobre la Renta de no Residentes for permanent establishments, filed electronically through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria electronic headquarters. Modelo 220 applies where the company is part of a Spanish tax-consolidated group.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is due within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year company closing on 31 December, the ordinary filing window is generally 1 to 25 July of the following year, subject to the applicable electronic-filing calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate tax identification number, legal name, registered office, tax year dates, activity classification, tax domicile, turnover indicators, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the Spanish permanent establishment, Spanish tax representative where required, and the non-resident head office. A non-resident without a Spanish permanent establishment generally does not file Modelo 200 for ordinary Spanish-source income; withholding and Modelo 210 or other relevant forms may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before tax based on statutory accounts prepared under Spanish accounting rules or an accepted equivalent accounting framework.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A permanent establishment must attribute to Spain the income, expenses, assets, risks, and functions properly connected with the Spanish establishment and maintain supporting accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and deductions for non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, provisions, impairment, financial expenses, tax-exempt income, valuation adjustments, hybrid mismatches, and other statutory modifications.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply only adjustments attributable to the Spanish taxable presence. Transactions with the non-resident head office must be supported by allocation keys and arm's-length documentation where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose or reflect adjustments arising from related-party transactions, including purchases, sales, services, financing, royalties, guarantees, and business restructurings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use arm's-length pricing and retain local-file, master-file, country-by-country, valuation, and benefit evidence where documentation thresholds or group reporting rules apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Use available tax losses subject to statutory utilization limits, ownership-change restrictions, anti-abuse rules, and any applicable minimum-tax-base provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A permanent establishment may use only losses legally attributable to its Spanish taxable business. Imported or head-office losses cannot be deducted unless a specific statutory rule permits the deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim qualifying R&D, technological innovation, employment, audiovisual, cultural, environmental, and other statutory credits with required certificates, reports, and expenditure schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident owner cannot generally claim Spanish company-level credits unless the relevant expenditure and activity are incurred by the Spanish taxable entity or permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the taxable base, apply the relevant rate, deduct payments on account and withholding credits, and determine the final amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an SL, apply the resident-company regime unless a special regime applies. Check eligibility for the 15% newly incorporated or start-up rate before applying it.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Withholdings, payments on account, and instalments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile withholding credits and Modelo 202 corporate-tax instalments against the annual liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile only amounts legally withheld or paid for the Spanish entity or permanent establishment. Foreign tax credits require evidence of foreign tax paid and compliance with statutory limitation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Related-party disclosure and tax group information
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report tax-group membership, special regimes, related-party information, transactions subject to documentation, and other mandatory disclosures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the ultimate parent, foreign related parties, cross-border payments, beneficial ownership information, and applicable treaty or EU relief positions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Submit using an approved electronic certificate or authorized representative and pay through the authorized banking or electronic payment channel.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign shareholder or parent should appoint an authorized Spanish representative where necessary and retain the electronic filing receipt, payment reference, and filed XML or PDF record.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without tax payable may trigger a fixed penalty generally ranging from EUR 100 to EUR 200, subject to reduction where applicable. Late filing with tax payable generally triggers a surcharge of 1% for each complete month of delay during the first 12 months, with a higher surcharge after 12 months and late-payment interest. Incorrect or incomplete returns may attract tax sanctions generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid or improperly claimed tax, subject to aggravating and mitigating factors. Failure to make corporate-tax instalment payments may generate interest, surcharges, and sanctions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, corporate income tax payments on account, filed electronically through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria electronic headquarters. Modelo 222 applies to tax-consolidated groups.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Normally filed during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December. For large taxpayers or specific electronic-payment arrangements, the applicable filing calendar and payment mechanics must be checked separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number, legal name, tax year, instalment period, and applicable calculation method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident permanent establishment files only in relation to its Spanish taxable activity. A foreign shareholder without Spanish corporate-tax residence normally does not file Modelo 202.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the instalment by reference to the previous year's assessed corporate-tax liability, excluding certain credits and withholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the prior-period liability attributable to the Spanish taxpayer or permanent establishment and verify whether a shortened or newly incorporated tax year changes the calculation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: For taxpayers required or electing to use the current-period method, calculate the instalment based on the taxable income generated during the relevant period and apply statutory adjustments and rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support the calculation with interim accounts, transfer-pricing adjustments, permanent-establishment attribution schedules, and evidence for exempt or excluded income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct qualifying credits, withholdings, payments on account, and other legally available offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign taxes are creditable only under the statutory foreign-tax-credit rules and cannot be used without appropriate certificates and calculation support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the instalment amount and complete electronic payment or direct-debit instructions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the payment account and electronic certificate correspond to the Spanish taxpayer or duly authorized representative.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete instalment payments may produce collection surcharges, late-payment interest, and sanctions for failure to make required payments on account. Errors that understate the instalment may be sanctioned where culpability and a tax shortfall are established.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends and other profit distributions to non-residents, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. A qualifying EU parent company may obtain a full exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive implementation, generally requiring at least 10% direct ownership, a minimum holding period, subject-to-tax and legal-form conditions, and anti-abuse compliance. The domestic participation exemption for a Spanish corporate recipient may also apply subject to statutory conditions and a 5% taxation inclusion rule.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence issued by the recipient's competent foreign tax authority, verify beneficial ownership and treaty eligibility, apply the treaty rate where administratively permitted, and retain the payment ledger, ownership evidence, dividend resolution, treaty analysis, and anti-abuse substantiation. If the payer cannot apply the reduced rate at source, withhold at the domestic rate and pursue a refund through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria using the applicable non-resident tax refund procedure. The residence certificate must remain valid under Spanish administrative practice and should be renewed when required.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Spanish withholding is generally 24% for royalties and other qualifying income obtained by non-residents without a Spanish permanent establishment, and 19% for interest. Treaty rates vary by recipient country and treaty article. EU-interest and royalty relief may reduce withholding to zero where the EU associated-company conditions, minimum ownership, holding period, subject-to-tax, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse requirements are satisfied. Payments attributable to a Spanish permanent establishment are generally taxed through the permanent-establishment profit calculation rather than final withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Spain has no single universal transaction-value threshold that eliminates all transfer-pricing obligations. Local-file documentation is generally required for material related-party transactions, subject to statutory exemptions. A commonly applicable documentation exemption is an aggregate annual value not exceeding EUR 250,000 per related person or entity, measured by transaction type and subject to exclusions and conditions. Master-file obligations generally apply to Spanish entities or permanent establishments belonging to an international group, subject to statutory scope and exemptions. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to groups meeting the EUR 750 million consolidated-revenue threshold.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other OECD-consistent methods and valuation techniques where the listed methods cannot be reliably applied
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain has no separate regime formally titled Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. Substance is nevertheless decisive under Spanish and EU anti-abuse rules, including beneficial-ownership requirements, the principal-purpose test in treaties, the general anti-abuse rule, controlled foreign company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation rules, exit-tax rules, and EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive anti-abuse provisions. The SL should maintain Spanish decision-making, personnel, premises, manufacturing capability, quality systems, inventory controls, risk management, board records, and commercially substantiated functions for its intraocular-lens manufacturing activity. Conduit dividends, circular financing, unsupported royalties, and profit allocations inconsistent with functions and risks are high-risk positions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and false tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, inflating deductible expenses, fabricating invoices, omitting intra-group income, manipulating inventory, or knowingly submitting materially false corporate-tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax sanctions may generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, with interest and recovery costs. Serious tax fraud may constitute a criminal offense where statutory monetary and intent thresholds are met, with imprisonment generally ranging from one to five years and fines linked to the defrauded amount; aggravated cases may attract higher imprisonment and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil liability for tax debts and sanctions where they caused, tolerated, or failed to prevent the breach, and may face criminal liability as perpetrators, accomplices, or cooperating officers. Courts may impose asset seizure, restitution, disqualification from management, and imprisonment. Travel bans are not an automatic tax sanction but may be ordered by a court in criminal proceedings where legally justified.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Value-added tax fraud and carousel arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or using fictitious invoices, claiming input VAT without genuine supplies, misclassifying intra-Community supplies, or participating in missing-trader structures involving medical-device components or finished lenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT repayment, assessment of unpaid VAT, interest, and administrative sanctions commonly calculated as a percentage of the improperly deducted or unpaid amount. Serious or organized fraud may result in criminal prosecution, imprisonment, fines, asset seizure, and business disqualification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and financial officers may be personally liable where they knowingly participated in or authorized the scheme. Criminal courts may order restitution, confiscation, management disqualification, and imprisonment; travel restrictions depend on judicial orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's-length prices for lenses, tooling, contract manufacturing, technical services, royalties, guarantees, or intercompany financing to shift Spanish profits to a low-tax affiliate without functional and economic support.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may make a primary adjustment, impose secondary adjustments, deny deductions, assess withholding tax, and apply documentation and tax sanctions. Transfer-pricing penalties may be based on undisclosed or incorrectly documented data and may be accompanied by interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for intentional or negligent tax damage and criminal liability if the adjustment forms part of deliberate tax fraud. A corporate veil may be pierced only under applicable statutory or judicial doctrines; imprisonment is not automatic and requires criminal findings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, conduit, and beneficial-ownership abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SL solely as a conduit for dividends, royalties, interest, or invoice flows while lacking personnel, assets, manufacturing capacity, commercial decision-making, or genuine risk assumption in Spain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Treaty, EU, and domestic exemptions may be denied; withholding may be reassessed at domestic rates; deductions may be denied; anti-abuse provisions may apply; and interest and sanctions may follow. Sham transactions may generate criminal exposure where tax-fraud thresholds are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for knowingly implementing artificial arrangements and may face civil restitution, tax sanctions, asset seizure, disqualification, and criminal imprisonment if the conduct satisfies criminal tax or fraud offenses. Judicial travel restrictions may be imposed in appropriate criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify beneficial owners, accepting unexplained SWIFT payments or letters of credit, processing high-risk-country funds without enhanced due diligence, structuring payments, or failing to report suspicious transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish AML breaches may attract substantial administrative fines, public censure, temporary prohibitions, and management disqualification. Serious money laundering or terrorist-financing conduct may lead to criminal fines, confiscation, corporate dissolution or suspension, and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and authorized signatories may be personally liable for knowing participation, consent, or grossly negligent control failures. Courts may order restitution, confiscation, management disqualification, and imprisonment; travel bans may arise from judicial precautionary measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manufacturing, importing, placing on the EU market, or distributing intraocular lenses without required conformity assessment, CE marking, technical documentation, quality-management controls, traceability, vigilance procedures, or authorization from the competent Spanish authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Authorities may order corrective actions, product withdrawal or recall, suspension or closure of facilities, license restrictions, administrative fines, and liability for patient or customer damage. Serious harm, falsification, or knowingly unsafe products may lead to criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil compensation liability and criminal liability for knowingly placing unsafe or non-compliant medical devices on the market. Courts may impose fines, imprisonment, disqualification, confiscation, and precautionary travel restrictions where legally justified.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining off-book accounts, falsifying production yields or inventory, backdating shareholder resolutions, concealing related-party balances, or approving accounts that materially misrepresent the SL's financial position.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Possible consequences include accounting corrections, tax reassessment, administrative penalties, civil claims, insolvency-related liability, and criminal sanctions for false accounting, corporate fraud, or creditor prejudice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal civil liability, insolvency clawback, disqualification from administration, restitution, asset seizure, and imprisonment where criminal elements are established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared cross-border payments and withholding failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, interest, management fees, or technical-service charges to non-residents without correct withholding, treaty verification, beneficial-owner analysis, or required reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The SL may owe the unwithheld tax, interest, reporting penalties, and sanctions. Treaty relief may be denied where residence certificates, beneficial ownership, holding periods, or anti-abuse evidence are deficient.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be secondarily liable under Spanish tax-liability rules where they caused or failed to remedy the withholding breach. Deliberate concealment may create criminal tax exposure, with restitution, fines, disqualification, and imprisonment subject to the statutory thresholds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Insolvency, creditor prejudice, and unlawful distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits without distributable reserves, extracting assets before insolvency, paying related parties while creditors remain unpaid, or continuing operations after a statutory dissolution or insolvency trigger without taking required action.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences may include repayment of unlawful distributions, damages, insolvency clawback, director disqualification, liability for the insolvency deficit, and criminal sanctions for asset concealment or creditor fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for restitution, creditor compensation, the insolvency deficit, asset seizure, management disqualification, and imprisonment where criminal conduct is proven. Courts may impose precautionary travel restrictions in criminal or insolvency proceedings.
